newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay blue-chips rally, index up 1.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bombay blue-chips rally, index up 1.5 pct.

text.p: ** (0645 GMT) Multinational stocks lead rally in Bombay shares
** Benchmark Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index jumps 65.36
points, or 1.52 percent, to 4,371.75 by mid-session
Bombay shares rose by mid-session on Wednesday behind a surge in multinational stocks fancied by foreign institutional investors (FIIs), brokers said.
"FIIs are pumping money into side counters, mainly multinational stocks," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
He said fund managers were shifting their focus to other blue-chips after buying into index-linked stocks.

Atlas Copco, Asea Brown, Cadbury's, Castrol, Colgate, Hindustan Lever, P&G, SKF Bearings, SmithKline Beecham Pharmaceuticals, Siemens, Sandvik Asia and Hindustan Ciba-Giegy were some of the multinational shares that rose sharply.
